correctness.rationale: PASS: Every B_r is bipartite and of diameter three. In any bipartite graph, distances from a third vertex to adjacent endpoints differ by exactly one, so an edge plus a third selected vertex violates the geodesic general-position condition. Conversely, independence forces any path via another selected vertex to have length at least 4, impossible for a geodesic in B_r. Split independent sets into neither spine vertex and exactly x or y: I(B_r;t)=(1+2t)^r+2t(1+t)^r; restore all 3r+1 missing adjacent pairs, because every 2-set is in general position. The coefficient q_k=2^k*C(r,k)+2*C(r,k-1) has an explicit strictly positive normalized q_k²-q_(k-1)q_(k+1) polynomial in k,n=r-k from the pinned proof; independently reconstructed this polynomial identity in exact sympy and checked inequalities r=2..49. Raising q_2 only requires separate k=1,2,3 inequalities, all given positive factorizations, with r=2 endpoint handled. This proves strict log-concavity for all r analytically. The highest degree is r+1 with coefficient 2, establishing exact maxima. The original enumeration script was inspected; its r=2..8 exhaustive outputs support but do not prove the parameter-unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: PASS: Square-page book graphs form a standard named infinite family and a natural bipartite Cartesian product. Its exact all-size general-position set generating function, the all-large-set independence equivalence and coefficientwise strict log-concavity answer a motivated polynomial unimodality question considerably beyond the previously known scalar gp or dual GP number. This is not a relabelled enumeration of a previously published polynomial.

final_claim: For every r>=2, the square-page book B_r formed by r C4 cycles sharing edge xy has general position polynomial psi(B_r;t)=(1+2t)^r+2t(1+t)^r+(3r+1)t². All general position sets of cardinality >=3 are exactly the independent sets. Its positive coefficients are strictly log-concave; the maximal size is r+1 and exactly the two bipartition classes achieve it.
limitations: r>=2 only, not triangular or longer-cycle books, nor arbitrary theta graphs or K_(1,r) box H.
Independent symbolic identities and finite r checks corroborate, whereas the proof of positivity covers every r.
Full general-position polynomial and dual-general-position polynomial are distinct invariants.
